trigger: Boeing launches a clean-sheet single-aisle (b737next, variant cleansheet)
response: Against the 787 we did not concede. We answered with our own new airplane (the relaunched A350), arriving 2-3 years behind, and bridged with aggressive pricing of the older product. Here the neo is already the bridge. We expect a Boeing clean sheet to slip beyond its announced date (inference from Boeing's 787 record).
lag: 2-3 years (A350 against 787); for the neo, same turn: hold
war_game_translation: Keep a320neo, launched or launching in 2010. No cancel. Public statement claims the in-service lead. Use whatif to add 1-2 years of slip to Boeing's clean sheet.

response: No direct precedent in the evidence. Our revealed intent is to gain share and not sit still. A like-for-like Boeing answer takes 6 years against our 5 (engine), so we keep the lead.
war_game_translation: Keep a320neo. No cancel. Engine choice by the section 9 test (tie within $0.3B: cfm_leap for capture).

response: We keep ramping and taking share. Boeing's stated alternative to re-engining is incremental NG improvement, 5% fuel so far and 2% coming.
war_game_translation: Launch a320neo in 2010 (Turn 1), then no new moves. Do not delay to reduce A350 strain unless the section 9 waiting test is met.

response: We ramped faster than Boeing on similar orders (high 30s against low 30s) and were raising narrowbody rates in parallel in 2010, competing for the same suppliers.
war_game_translation: No rate lever in this scenario. Hold the neo; do not cancel. Say in the public statement that we are raising rates too. Predict rate_increase: true in Turn 1.

trigger: Boeing re-engines, upgrades or stretches a widebody (777 changes, 787-10)
response: We widened our family to cover two Boeing lines with one airplane and marketed its performance aggressively (A350-1000).
war_game_translation: No widebody lever in this scenario. Neo orders unchanged.

trigger: Boeing price aggression or order-campaign losses
response: We priced older products aggressively to hold customers until the newer product arrived. Our own announced price increases did not stick.
war_game_translation: Pricing is not a lever. Never cancel because of lost campaigns. Do not disclose price commitments.

trigger: Boeing acquires or partners (for example a regional-jet maker, or a CSeries-type entrant)
response: No record of our response. Boeing notes Embraer and Bombardier moving up in size and new entrants targeting 70-190 seats.
war_game_translation: We have no Joint Venture lever here. Note it in the rationale; do not change neo orders.

trigger: Boeing stumbles (787 delays, 747-8 charges, the More 787 setbacks inject)
response: We marketed our own new airplane's capabilities harder. Boeing itself admits the 787 plan outran its ability to execute.
war_game_translation: Hold the plan. The inject raises Boeing's strain; that argues against Boeing launching quickly, not for us waiting.

trigger: Demand shock or downturn (Eurozone downturn inject)
response: We leaned more on export-credit agencies (45% of 2010 deliveries, against 35% in 2009) to hold deliveries. We carried less over-ordering cushion than Boeing (inference).
war_game_translation: Do not cancel or defer the neo for a two-year dip. Re-run whatif with the inject applied.

trigger: Weak dollar or cost pressure on our margins
response: We cut overhead, shortened the development cycle and raised productivity through 2012, then used the gains for product development, price-led share or earnings.
war_game_translation: Cost pressure is not a reason to delay the neo launch.

trigger: Supply-chain or engine problems (ours or shared suppliers)
response: We ran a dispersed, hard-to-manage production footprint and absorbed program delays (A380 wiring). Boeing expects us to hit 787-type problems on new programs.
war_game_translation: Test 0-1 year of neo slip in whatif. No cancel for a slip alone. Never disclose EIS before 2015.

trigger: Regulatory or trade action (WTO, procurement protests)
response: No record of our response. Boeing litigates: it welcomed the 2010 WTO ruling against launch aid and filed a tanker protest within 11 days. Boeing argues subsidies let us take more risk.
war_game_translation: Fund the neo without new launch aid, to give Boeing no new trade target (inference). No order change.

trigger: Fuel spike, order boom, or a loyal Boeing customer splitting an order (injects)
response: Boeing reported customers pushing for re-engined or new airplanes because of fuel prices. We pursue share when demand favours us.
war_game_translation: Each strengthens holding the neo; none flips it. Use in the public statement.
